newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico closes two ports in stormy weather.
newsitem.headline: Mexico closes two ports in stormy weather.

text.p: Two Mexican ports were closed Friday to shipping as stormy weather once again hit southern Mexico, the Communications and Transportation Ministry said.

In a statement, the ministry said Salina Cruz and Coatzacoalcos were closed. Salina Cruz is a minor crude port on the Pacific side serving Far East markets and Coatzacoalcos is the Gulf terminal that has jurisdiction over Pajaritos, one of Mexico's three main crude ports.
The statement did not say directly that Pajaritos was closed but the captain in the Veracruz port normally closes both ports together.
A spokeswoman from the state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said later that all the main three Gulf oil ports were open to shipping.
"All three are totally open," she said, refering to Pajaritos, Dos Bocas and Cayo Arcas -- the terminals that handle crude for the United States and European markets.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
